features/annotate-screenshots.bodyHtml:
Explain the screenshot without a long message

Skreen includes 13 annotation tools for marking up a capture. Use an arrow to point to a control, text to label a state, or a shape to outline a region. Measurement and other marks help with design feedback when the exact position or size matters.

A simple annotation workflow

  1. Capture the relevant area, window, or scrolling page.
  2. Add one or two marks that answer the reader’s first question: where should I look, and what changed?
  3. Keep labels short and use a consistent color when you have several steps.
  4. Check whether the image contains account names, private messages, or credentials. Cover those details before export.

For a bug report, capture the broken state and mark the control or message that triggered it. For a tutorial, use numbered captures in a combined composition when one image cannot show the whole flow.

Keep the original message visible

Annotations should guide attention, not obscure the interface you are trying to show. Crop first, keep marks outside important text where possible, and review the final export at the size your reader will see.

features/beautiful-backgrounds.title: Beautiful Screenshot Backgrounds for Mac — Skreen
features/beautiful-backgrounds.description: Give Mac screenshots a polished background in Skreen with gradients, patterns, wallpapers, framing, and Auto-Beautify color suggestions.

features/beautiful-backgrounds.lead: Turn a raw capture into an image that is ready for a document, release note, or presentation. Choose a background, frame, shadow, and size without leaving Skreen.

related.title: Annotate screenshots
related.body: Add a useful explanation to the image.

features/beautiful-backgrounds.bodyHtml:
Pick a look that fits the content

Skreen offers 48 curated gradient presets and 13 procedural patterns. You can also use a custom gradient or a desktop wallpaper, including your current wallpaper and installed macOS wallpapers. Auto-Beautify can suggest a treatment based on the colors in your screenshot.

From raw capture to finished image

  1. Capture an area or window and open it in the editor.
  2. Choose a background that keeps the screenshot readable. Add a frame or shadow if it helps separate the interface from the background.
  3. Set the aspect ratio for where the image will appear, such as a presentation slide or a social post.
  4. Review the export at its intended size. Skreen can export at the source image’s native pixel density for a sharper result.

A bright background can be useful for product announcements. For dense text, use a quiet color and enough padding so the content remains the focus. You can annotate the same capture before exporting.

Before and after: a release-note image

The raw capture shows a browser or app window edge to edge. For the finished version, place that same capture on a quiet background, add padding around it, and use a restrained frame or shadow to separate the window from the page. Judge legibility in the editor preview before export. Keep small interface text readable at the final size; a decorative background cannot fix an overly reduced capture.

related.title: Beautiful backgrounds
related.body: Give the layout a consistent finish.

features/combine-screenshots.bodyHtml:
Choose a layout for the story

Use a grid when the images should have equal weight, such as several steps in a workflow. Use Free Canvas when you want to place captures at different sizes or positions. Skreen can add a new capture to an existing composition, so you can build the image as you work.

Build a clear comparison

  1. Capture the first state and add it to a composition.
  2. Capture the next state, or add another existing capture.
  3. Align the images so the reader can compare the same region in each one. Add short annotations to identify the change.
  4. Apply a consistent background and spacing, then export a single image.

If the source images have different sizes, preview the composition at the final display size. Small UI text may become hard to read when several full-screen captures are squeezed into one canvas; crop each frame to the relevant area first.

Example: a two-state bug report

Place a capture of the expected state next to the broken state in a two-column grid. Crop both to the same control, then add a short label above each one. The reader can compare the change without switching between files. If one state needs more room, move the captures to Free Canvas and size them independently. Export the composition as one image only after checking that both labels and the relevant UI are legible.

features/ocr-and-qr.title: Copy Text and QR Codes from Screenshots on Mac — Skreen
features/ocr-and-qr.description: Extract text and read QR codes from Mac screenshots with Skreen's Apple Vision recognition tools, built into the capture workflow.
features/ocr-and-qr.h1: Get the information out of the image.
features/ocr-and-qr.lead: When you need a line of text or a QR destination, Skreen can recognize it from a capture on your Mac so you do not have to retype it.

related.title: How to screenshot on Mac
related.body: Start with the right capture shortcut.

features/ocr-and-qr.bodyHtml:
Capture text without retyping

Use Skreen’s Capture Text action when the text itself is all you need. You can also recognize text from an image already open in the editor. Recognition uses Apple’s Vision framework on your device.

For example, capture an error message from an app, copy it as text, and paste it into a support ticket. You can still save the image when the visual context matters.

Copy text step by step

  1. Capture the line or open an existing screenshot in Skreen.
  2. Use Capture Text or the editor’s text recognition action.
  3. Compare the recognized text against the image, especially punctuation, numbers, and line breaks.
  4. Copy the text into your document or support ticket. Keep the screenshot with it when the original layout helps explain the problem.

Read a QR code from a capture

Skreen can detect QR codes in captured content. Review the recognized destination before opening or sharing it, just as you would with any link from an unfamiliar source.

For example, if a QR code appears in a presentation slide, capture that region and read the destination in Skreen before deciding whether to visit it. Check the actual URL rather than relying on the surrounding label.

Check the result

OCR accuracy depends on the image. Tiny text, low contrast, unusual fonts, and overlapping UI can produce mistakes. Compare the recognized text with the screenshot before you rely on it for a command, address, or important number. If the image contains private data, redact it before sharing.

features/redact-screenshots.bodyHtml:
Find details before they leave your Mac

Skreen uses Apple Vision on your device to look for faces and sensitive text. Detection covers email addresses, phone numbers, card numbers, IP addresses, API keys, passwords, US Social Security numbers, and custom patterns you define. You can also select an area yourself when automatic detection misses something.

How to redact a screenshot

  1. Take a screenshot or open a capture in the Skreen editor.
  2. Run sensitive-data detection and inspect the proposed matches. Add or adjust selections where needed.
  3. Choose blur, pixelation, or a solid cover for each area. Use the manual selection for anything the detector did not identify.
  4. Zoom in and check the full image, including edges and background content, before exporting the file you intend to share.

For text, the Alt key can snap a selection to word boundaries. This makes it easier to cover a single token without hiding the surrounding explanation.

What changes between capture and export

Imagine a bug report showing a payment form. In the unedited capture, the field values sit beside the error you need to explain. Cover the card number with a solid block while keeping the form labels and surrounding interface visible. Check the exported file: the private value should be unreadable, and the evidence for the bug should still be clear.

Choose the right cover

Blur or pixelation can make a design review easier to read while obscuring an incidental name or face. For secrets such as passwords, API keys, and payment details, a solid cover is the clearer choice. Automated detection is a helper, so always review the exported image yourself before sharing sensitive material.

features/scrolling-screenshots.bodyHtml:
How to take a scrolling screenshot

  1. Open the page or scrollable view and bring the part you want to capture into view.
  2. Start a scrolling capture in Skreen and select the content area. Keep the selection inside the scrolling region so fixed browser chrome is left out.
  3. Start scrolling. You can pause, change direction, resume, or cancel while capturing. Finish when you have reached the end of the section you need.
  4. Review the stitched image in the editor. Crop extra space, add an annotation, or hide private details before you export.

Skreen combines overlapping frames and works to avoid repeating elements that stay fixed while the content moves. The result is one image, so a reader can follow the page from top to bottom without opening several files.

If macOS asks for Screen Recording access during the first capture, open System Settings, grant Skreen the requested access, and return to the app. macOS may ask you to restart the app before the new permission takes effect. Choose only the content you intend to capture; browser tabs and conversations can include private information outside the visible area.

When it helps

Use scrolling capture for a long article, a support conversation, a design review, a document, or a bug report where the content extends beyond one screen. If you only need what is visible right now, an area or window capture is quicker.

What to check before sharing

Dynamic content can change while a page scrolls. Animations, expanding panels, and lazy-loaded sections may produce a different image from a static page. Keep the view steady, let content load, and review the final stitch before sending it. Scrolling capture works best when the content moves inside a clearly selected scroll area.

Scrolling capture questions

Why is part of the page repeated or missing?

Moving banners, autoplay video, sticky elements, or content that loads during the scroll can interrupt the stitch. Let the page settle, select the actual scrolling region, and try a shorter capture. Inspect the exported image rather than assuming every frame joined cleanly.

Can I capture a long chat or document?

Yes, when its content scrolls inside a selectable region. Start with a short section to confirm the result, then capture the full portion you need. If the view does not scroll consistently, use separate area captures and combine them.

guides/how-to-screenshot-on-mac.bodyHtml:
The built-in Mac screenshot shortcuts

What you want Shortcut What happens
The entire screen Shift–Command–3 macOS captures the screen.
A selected area Shift–Command–4 Drag the crosshair over the area you need.
A window or menu Shift–Command–4, then Space Move the camera over a window and click.
Screenshot controls Shift–Command–5 Open the Screenshot app to choose a capture or recording mode.

These are macOS shortcuts; you can use them without installing Skreen. Apple’s screenshot guide also explains where the resulting files are saved and how the Screenshot app’s options work.

If the page is longer than one screen

A standard area or window screenshot captures what is visible. For a long page, document, or scrollable view, use Skreen’s scrolling capture: select the content region, scroll through the part you need, and finish with one stitched image. Check the final image before sharing, especially if the page contains animation or content that loads as you scroll.

Make the screenshot ready to share

Use annotations to point to the relevant button or problem. Add a background when presentation matters. If the capture contains personal information, use redaction and inspect the export. Skreen can also extract text and QR codes from a capture.

If a native macOS shortcut already produces the file you need, you can stop there. Use Skreen when you need the extra capture and editing steps together.

faq.question: Can Skreen capture a page that is longer than my screen?
faq.answer: Yes. Select the scrollable area, scroll through the content you need, then review the stitched image before exporting it.

faq.question: Are my screenshots uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Captures, editing, text recognition, and sensitive-data detection run on your Mac.

faq.question: Can I combine several screenshots into one image?
faq.answer: Yes. Arrange captures in a grid or freely on a canvas, then export the finished composition.

faq.question: Can I copy text from a screenshot?
faq.answer: Yes. Skreen recognizes text in images on your Mac so you can copy the words you need.

faq.question: Can I change the background of a screenshot?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose a Mac wallpaper, a solid color, or a custom gradient, then adjust the spacing and frame in the editor.

faq.question: What version of macOS do I need?
faq.answer: Skreen requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later.
